title: U.S. House · Indiana's 1st District
area: Northwest Indiana, including Gary, Hammond, Merrillville and Valparaiso (Lake, Porter, and part of LaPorte counties)

context.text: Incumbent Frank Mrvan won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over LaVetta Sparks-Wade. Barb Regnitz won a contested Republican primary over David Ben Ruiz and James Schenke.
Two independent write-in candidates, Alexander Degman and James Johnson, are also on Ballotpedia's list for the general election.

candidates.name: Frank Mrvan
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over LaVetta Sparks-Wade

summary.text: Frank Mrvan is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Indiana's 1st District, first elected in 2020 and seeking a fourth term. A former mortgage broker and pharmaceutical sales representative, he served as North Township trustee for 15 years before Congress. He sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Hammond, Indiana; graduated from Morton High School (1987) and earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Ball State University (1992).
Worked as a licensed mortgage broker and pharmaceutical sales representative before entering elected office.
Appointed North Township trustee in November 2005 when his predecessor resigned, and served in that office until 2021, a total his official biography describes as 15 years.

Announced his candidacy for Congress in 2020 after Rep. Pete Visclosky decided not to seek re-election. Won a 14-candidate Democratic primary with 33% of the vote and defeated Republican Mark Leyva in the general election, 57% to 40%.
Took office January 3, 2021. Re-elected in 2022 over Republican Jennifer-Ruth Green and in 2024 over Republican Randy Niemeyer, and defeated LaVetta Sparks-Wade in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress serves on the House Appropriations Committee and its Commerce, Justice, Science and Energy and Water Development subcommittees, and is vice chairman of the Congressional Steel Caucus.
Earlier House assignments included the Veterans' Affairs Committee (chairing its Technology Modernization subcommittee in 2021–22) and the Education and the Workforce Committee.
According to his official biography, he is married to Jane and they have two daughters.

priorities.text: Serves as Vice Chairman of the Congressional Steel Caucus in the 119th Congress.
Lists improving access to affordable healthcare, including prescription drug costs and veterans' mental health services, as a top priority.
Describes support for public schools, teachers, and students as a continuing focus, citing his prior service on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.
Cites organized labor as central to the Northwest Indiana economy and says he supports it.

positions.summary: Wrote to DHS opposing a proposed ICE detention facility in Merrillville, citing civil-liberties concerns, while saying he opposes open borders and that people apprehended committing crimes should receive due process and be prosecuted.
positions.quote: I strongly oppose any plan to convert a commercial warehouse in Indiana’s First Congressional District into an ICE detention facility.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Appropriations (Commerce-Justice-Science and Energy-Water Development subcommittees) for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Education and the Workforce during the 117th and 118th Congresses (2021-2024).
Chaired the Technology Modernization Subcommittee of the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs during the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

candidates.name: Barb Regnitz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over David Ben Ruiz and James Schenke

summary.text: Barb Regnitz is a Porter County Commissioner and the Republican nominee for Indiana's 1st District. She worked as a software engineer and project manager before becoming a Certified Financial Planner, and was elected commissioner in 2022. Her campaign emphasizes border security, reduced federal spending and public safety.

background.text: Holds a bachelor's degree from Purdue University.
Worked as a computer programmer and business analyst for the Woolworth Company and as a software engineer and project manager for United Airlines.

Became a financial advisor and Certified Financial Planner with A.G. Edwards and Raymond James; her campaign says that career taught her "the value of fiscal responsibility, transparency and careful decision-making."
Elected Porter County Commissioner in 2022; in her survey she says she focuses on public safety, infrastructure and county facilities.
Was one of three Republicans in the May 5, 2026 primary, alongside Ben Ruiz and Jim Schenke, and is the Republican candidate on the November ballot.
Serves on the boards of the Valparaiso Rotary Club, Valparaiso Rotary Foundation and the LaSalle Council of Scouting America, and is treasurer of the Rotary Foundation and SCORE.
According to her survey, she lives in Valparaiso with her husband, Tim.

priorities.text: Lists border security, reducing government spending, and public safety ("Safe Cities") as her three key campaign messages.
priorities.quote: Border Security: Strengthen border security to stop illegal crossings, drugs, and human trafficking. ... Smarter Spending: Strengthen Americans' purchasing power by ending reckless spending and curbing inflation. ... Safe Cities: Enforce the law by ensuring criminals are arrested, prosecuted, and held accountable for their actions.

priorities.text: Says she is personally passionate about taxes, education, the national debt, and secure borders.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for reserving girls' sports and facilities in schools by sex.
positions.quote: Protect fairness and safety in schools by keeping girls' sports and facilities reserved for biological females.

statements.quote: Reform immigration policies to prioritize safety, legal entry, and accountability.
statements.context: On her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia

statements.quote: Support law enforcement with the resources and respect they need to keep our communities safe.
statements.context: On her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia

James Johnson is an independent write-in candidate for Indiana's 1st Congressional District. Ballotpedia's general-election list has no additional biographical detail on him.

researchNotes: No public campaign website was located for Barb Regnitz beyond the text captured in her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign-website excerpt, so her website field is left blank; she did not return the Indiana Capital Chronicle questionnaire. Independent write-in candidates Alexander Degman and James Johnson have no discoverable public statements (a BallotReady profile for Degman has only his name); entries are marked minimal. Lakeshore Public Media lists barbregnitzforcongress.com as Barb Regnitz's campaign site, but it could not be loaded here, so her biography relies on her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and that news guide, and her website field is left blank. Little biographical detail beyond ballot status could be found for Degman and Johnson, so their biographies are not expanded.
